title: Invertibility of the fixed-locus conormal Euler operator
statement:
For an affine finite-type group scheme $G$ over a field $F$ [def-weil-field, def-sc-group-scheme] acting on an $F$-scheme $Y$ [def-pc-scheme], a $G$-linearized coherent module means a coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module [pqf-def-coherent] with an isomorphism $a^*\mathcal M\simeq\operatorname{pr}_2^*\mathcal M$ on $G\times_FY$, satisfying the identity and cocycle identities; its geometric fibre action is from $y$ to $gy$. Let $G_0^G(Y)$ be the abelian group on isomorphism classes of these modules, with relations $[\mathcal M]=[\mathcal M']+[\mathcal M'']$ for every equivariant short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal M'\to\mathcal M\to\mathcal M''\to0$. Let $R(G)$ be the analogous group of finite-dimensional rational $G$-modules, with multiplication induced by tensor product. Rational means a counital coassociative coaction $V\to V\otimes_FF[G]$. Tensoring a sheaf with the trivial vector bundle associated to such a module makes $G_0^G(Y)$ an $R(G)$-module. Suppose $F$ is algebraically closed [def-weil-algebraic-closure], $G=T\simeq\mathbf G_m^r$ is a split torus for $r\geq0$ (where $\mathbf G_m(A)=A^\times$), and $Y$ is smooth and projective over $F$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-pc-morphism-conventions]. Suppose $i:W\hookrightarrow Y$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] representing the functor of points fixed after every commutative algebra extension. Let $\mathcal I$ be its ideal sheaf. Then $W$ is smooth over $F$ and $i$ is regular near $W$: each point of $W$ has an affine neighbourhood in $Y$ on which $\mathcal I$ is generated by a regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], and these lengths are bounded independently of the point. The conormal module $N^\vee=\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$ is locally finite free on $W$, with its induced $T$-linearization, and all its geometric fibre weights are nonzero. Put $X=\operatorname{Hom}(T,\mathbf G_m)$, $R=\mathbf Z[X]$ with $e^\eta e^\xi=e^{\eta+\xi}$, and let $\Sigma$ be generated by $1-e^\eta$ for $\eta\ne0$. On
$$M=G_0^T(W)\otimes_RR_\Sigma,$$
where $R$ acts by character twists, the alternating exterior tensor operator of [lem-sfb-equivariant-regular-self-intersection]
$$L([\mathcal M])=\sum_{q\geq0}(-1)^q[\bigwedge^qN^\vee\otimes_{\mathcal O_W}\mathcal M]$$
extended $R_\Sigma$-linearly is an automorphism. The sum is finite. This includes $W=\varnothing$ and the codimension-zero case, when $N^\vee=0$ and $L$ is the identity. It is an integer Grothendieck-group assertion in every characteristic.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-smooth-projective-torus-invariant-affine-cover] choose a finite invariant affine cover $U_j$ of $Y$. On each $U_j$, $W\cap U_j$ represents the fixed functor: a point factors through this fibre product exactly when its image is fixed in $Y$ and lies in $U_j$, and invariance makes this the fixed functor of the restricted action. Apply [lem-sfb-torus-fixed-scheme-smooth] to each $U_j$, then [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-local-on-source] to the covering $W\cap U_j$ of $W$. Thus $W$ is smooth, including the empty-cover case.

source.place: Theorem 13.1, pp.254--256; Definition 13.45 and Lemma 13.46, p.272, with the missing invariant-affine input stated separately.

proof.text: Projectivity makes $Y$ proper by [lem-pc-projective-proper]; its closed subscheme $W$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. Apply [lem-trf-proper-field-invertible-coherent] to each scheme with the invertible module $\mathcal O$: both schemes are Noetherian and quasi-compact. Their dimensions are finite by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]. The two smooth structure maps and the closed immersion meet precisely the hypotheses of [lem-pur-smooth-pair-regular-immersion], giving regular sequences near every point of $W$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-conormal-free] the conormal of each such affine presentation is free on those equations; [lem-sc-affine-conormal-frame] identifies these frames with frames of $\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$. Hence $N^\vee$ is locally finite free. A finite subcover of $W$ by these charts bounds all the lengths by their maximum. Pullback of the invariant ideal and its square supplies the induced linearization, since the action preserves both products and the quotient.

source.place: Tag 067U, lemma-immersion-smooth-into-smooth-regular-immersion; algebra.tex 00LN; morphisms.tex 01R3. Finite-subcover argument is elementary.

proof.text: The action on $W$ is trivial by its representing property on every algebra. At a closed point $w$ of an affine chart of $W$, [lem-wf-affine-nullstellensatz-vanishing](1) identifies the residue field with $F$. A tangent vector is a map from $\operatorname{Spec}F[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ reducing to $w$. The fixed-functor property says exactly that such vectors factoring through $W$ are the vectors fixed by $T$ after every algebra extension. Thus $T_wW=(T_wY)^T$. The conormal fibre sequence [lem-pur-conormal-sequence-smooth-immersion], dualized as finite-dimensional vector spaces, gives the equivariant exact sequence $0\to T_wW\to T_wY\to (N^\vee_w)^*\to0$. By [lem-sfb-split-torus-representation-weight-decomposition], taking the zero-weight component is exact (maps preserve each character component, so the ordinary kernel and image are computed componentwise). The first map is an isomorphism on zero weights, so $(N^\vee_w)^*$ has zero zero-weight part, and the same holds for $N^\vee_w$. Apply [lem-sfb-trivial-torus-coherent-weight-decomposition] to $N^\vee$ on $W$. Its zero-weight summand is a vector bundle with zero fibre at every closed point, hence is zero by that node. The same node says weight decomposition commutes with field extension, proving the assertion at every geometric fibre, not only the closed $F$-points.

source.place: Theorem 13.1 and the cotangent calculation in the proof of Lemma 13.6, pp.254--256; Stacks 06AA for the exact fibre sequence. Dual-number identification is written out here.

proof.text:
Use [lem-sfb-trivial-torus-coherent-weight-decomposition] to write $N^\vee=\bigoplus_{\eta\in\Omega}E_\eta\otimes e^\eta$ with finite $\Omega\subset X\setminus\{0\}$, and partition $W$ into finitely many clopen pieces on which every $n_\eta=\operatorname{rank}E_\eta$ is constant. The same node identifies the equivariant coherent groups with $G_0(W)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}R$, compatibly with tensor and with this partition. It is enough to invert $L$ on one nonempty piece $Z$, with $\dim Z\leq d$. Its exterior expansion gives
$$L=\sum_{(j_\eta)}(-1)^{\sum j_\eta}e^{\sum j_\eta\eta}\,T_{\bigotimes_\eta\wedge^{j_\eta}E_\eta}.$$
All terms have $0\leq j_\eta\leq n_\eta$. In particular $L$ is a finite sum of exact tensor operators, so respects every short exact sequence relation. The rank of the bundle in a term is $\prod_\eta\binom{n_\eta}{j_\eta}$ (compute in a local basis). Replacing every tensor operator by this rank therefore gives the scalar
$$c=\prod_{\eta\in\Omega}(1-e^\eta)^{n_\eta}.$$
This scalar is a unit in $R_\Sigma$, since all $\eta$ are nonzero. Set $D=L-c\,\mathrm{id}$. The displayed expansion expresses $D$ as a finite $R_\Sigma$-linear combination of tensor operators minus their ranks. By [lem-sfb-coherent-support-filtration-rank-action], $D^{d+1}=0$ on $G_0(Z)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}R_\Sigma$, the module identified with the required localized group by associativity of tensor products.

source.place: Agent assembly from 02S9, lemma-cycles-k-group, and groupoids.tex 0EKL. The finite exterior expansion and scalar binomial calculation are explicit.

proof.text:
Put $A=c^{-1}D$. The scalar $c$ commutes with $D$ by $R_\Sigma$-linearity, so $A^{d+1}=0$. Then
$$L^{-1}=c^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^d(-A)^k.$$
Indeed multiplication on either side by $L=c(1+A)$ telescopes to $1-(-A)^{d+1}=1$. Assemble these inverses across the finite clopen partition using step 4. If $W=\varnothing$, its coherent group is zero, and its only endomorphism is an automorphism. If $N^\vee=0$, the only exterior term is $\wedge^0N^\vee=\mathcal O_W$, so $L=1$. For $r=0$ every weight is zero, so step 3 forces $N^\vee=0$ and gives the same conclusion. No integer has been inverted: only the specified character factors have been inverted.
